entries.name: Agentic Commerce Protocol (ACP)
entries.status: Specification in beta, maintained by OpenAI and Stripe; MAINTAINERS.md also lists Meta (PR #236 "ADMIN: Add Meta as TSC member", merged 2026-04-24). Last dated version 2026-04-17; on 2026-10-13 main is still at commit 7fdd78d (2026-07-17), README badge "Beta", no tag or release (not found, 2026-10-13), and the directory spec/unreleased holds the changes not yet dated (checkout, cart, delegate, feed schemas and OpenAPI files).
entries.relevance: The README says ACP "is an interaction model and open standard for connecting buyers, their AI agents, and businesses to complete purchases seamlessly." and covers agentic checkout and delegated payment over Representational State Transfer (REST) and an MCP binding. The seller enters through the checkout session's required links field (terms, privacy, return, shipping) and the unreleased product feed, whose optional barcode has a type (GTIN, UPC or EAN) and a value; requests carry a Signature header; the order schema has a receipt_url. The discovery RFC says "Seller identity is established through authentication (Bearer token), which is unavailable at discovery time." The OpenAI developer documentation (developers.openai.com/commerce/specs/checkout, read 2026-10-14) is a text separate from the specification in the repository (spec/unreleased). It says "Building with the Agentic Commerce Protocol is open to all." and "Instant Checkout in ChatGPT is currently available to approved partners." It documents a cancel call for a checkout session, which answers 405 when the session is already canceled or completed, and an order object with a list of refunds (types store_credit and original_payment); the cancellation of a checkout session is thus not the cancellation or refund of a completed order. The page /commerce/specs/delegated-payment answered HTTP 404 on 2026-10-14.
entries.boundary: The discovery document states "Agent identity and authorization are separate concerns", leaving catalog discovery and agent registration outside it.

entries.name: Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
entries.status: Open protocol in the GitHub organisation google-agentic-commerce (Apache-2.0); latest release v0.2.0 of 2026-04-28, which "focuses on providing Human Not Present flows"; core specification donated to FIDO. Google announced the donation on 2026-04-28 ("We're donating Agent Payments Protocol to the FIDO Alliance"); the FIDO release of the same day places the work in its Payments Technical Working Group, where the Google and Mastercard contributions are "providing an initial foundation for these specifications", and announces an Agentic Authentication Technical Working Group. entries.name: Browser vendor positions on WebMCP (WebKit, Mozilla, Chrome, Edge)
entries.status: WebKit position issue #670 closed 2026-06-11 as "position: oppose"; Mozilla #1412 closed 2026-08-05 as "position: neutral". Chrome early preview 2026-02-10; Edge blog of 2026-09-21: implementation "is ready for testing".
entries.relevance: WebMCP lets a page expose tools to browsing agents; Chrome describes it as "a standard way for exposing structured tools, ensuring AI agents can perform actions on your site with increased speed, reliability, and precision". The WebKit reviewer wrote on 2026-06-03 "WebKit is **opposed** to this proposal due to the following concerns:", among them that "it has no consent or reversibility model for consequential actions". The Mozilla reviewer proposed a neutral position, writing that "in an adversarial setting there is a risk that sites will provide tools that do not match the experience of a user on the page". PayPal's blog of 2026-09-16 says it is "extending WebMCP support through the PayPal JavaScript SDK" for Store Sync merchants; the agent can search, prepare the cart and initiate checkout, and "The buyer is then handed off to PayPal to sign in, choose or confirm a funding source, review the transaction, and approve payment." PayPal reports, as its own results of a small sandbox benchmark: "Approximately 4.6 times less costly in model-inference usage", "Approximately twice as fast at the median", and "three structured tool calls via WebMCP instead of more than 30 interface-interaction steps" (self-reported). Shopify's developer changelog of 2026-09-28 says "Browser agents can now read and update Shopify checkouts using WebMCP tools for checkout", with get_checkout, update_checkout and complete_checkout ("Submit checkout after buyer confirmation"); the tools "don't expose a new API or require merchant configuration". entries.name: GS1-Conformant Resolver Standard 1.2.1
entries.status: Release 1.2.1 ratified August 2026 (standards page and PDF print no day); the archive page on ref.gs1.org lists "Published 19 August 2026".
entries.relevance: The standard links an entity identified by a GS1 Digital Link URI, which carries a key such as a GTIN or a Global Location Number (GLN), to multiple sources of related information "in a way that is machine-discoverable and machine-actionable" (section 1), for example product information pages, product data and service APIs (section 2). The query string "does not form part of the entity's identifier", and for a valid URI with no information the resolver returns a simple 404 Not Found (sections 2.12, 2.4.1). On success it "SHALL redirect to the default link unless there is information in the request that can be used to determine a better response" (section 2.6.1); the prose gives no status code for the redirect, and the flowchart in Figure 2-1 shows 307. With `linkType=linkset` or the Accept header `application/linkset+json` it does not redirect and returns the links as an RFC 9264 linkset, and a conformant resolver publishes a Resolver Description File at /.well-known/gs1resolver (sections 2.9, 2.10). The Log of Changes records that an earlier SHOULD to recognise schema.org terms "has been removed although, of course, resolvers MAY use such terms."
entries.boundary: Out of scope: identical targets or linksets across resolvers, and any particular behaviour for query string parameters.

entries.status: Charter text under discussion on the audit list and in mirjak/audit-bof-preparation; the BoF request lists "User e-commerce use case" in its proposed agenda (file updated 2026-09-18). The relationship with VCON is therefore under discussion, not decided, as of 2026-11-06. On 2026-10-23 a BoF proponent opened issue #64 of mirjak/audit-bof-preparation, "Adding an out-of-scope section?", which reads "Discussion is on-going on the list. Currently proposed items would be:" auditing of model training; interactive or real-time auditing of agent behavior; requirements on the auditing system itself; authorization and delegation mechanisms or extensions to OAuth; and how and when to create the records ("audit is focused on collection and correlation").
entries.relevance: AUDIT concerns audit information about agents and delegated systems, so it touches commerce wherever an agent acts for a buyer and a seller or payer later needs a record of what happened. The charter scope reads "The scope of such auditing is the observable behavior of agents, including user intent, agent or tool interactions, invoked or declined actions, exchanged data, and" Commerce, seller, merchant: not found in the charter text, 2026-10-02; repository example: "booking a hotel room" (issue #16). The BoF request lists under "Architecture overview und use cases (20 mins)" a "User e-commerce use case" and names no presenter; the architecture draft has no "e-commerce" text, and its use cases include a flight booked through a chain of agents and "Financial Transactions by Agents": "Agents may execute financial operations such as payments or procurement actions on behalf of users". The sentence on VCON was proposed on the list on 2026-10-05 by a BoF proponent, Mirja Kuehlewind ("VCON is considered a suitable record format and the audit group will work with the vcon group to ensure the specified format addresses the auditing") and accepted on 2026-10-06 by a participant ("I'm OK with this wording"); another participant proposed a variant in charter style. On 2026-10-06 Sumit Ahuja wrote that he and Iman Schrock are writing an expected-record draft, "We are aiming for the -00 before the IETF 127 cutoff", which "declares which records each participant in a cross-domain chain is expected to produce, what each establishes, and when an absent one becomes a finding"; Schrock listed six conformance cases for it (declaration integrity, all slots filled, bounded observed absence, incomplete observation, wrong or ineligible record, late record) and the claim boundary "no qualifying record was found in the declared sources by the cutoff". No text of that draft was read; it was announced on the list. Case 4 reads "An unavailable source, incomplete pagination or coverage, unresolved participant set, or open window produces an incomplete audit, never an absence finding." On 2026-10-07 the author of this map wrote a seventh case on the list at Schrock's request, "Wrong recipient or holder": a record produced by the right party but held only by another does not fill the slot, and if the declared holder's source cannot be checked the audit is incomplete; the example is the confirmation that an EU trader owes the consumer on a durable medium (Directive 2011/83/EU, Art. 8(7)), held only by the agent platform. a co-author of the draft replied the same day that the case "catches a distinction the six cases do not state clearly" and asked for it to be written in the same shape; the draft text has not been read. The text of PR #61 adds to deliverable 2: "For interaction records - the expectation is that the group will leverage the VCON format. Extensions to VCON to add data needed to model AI" On 2026-10-07 a participant proposed case 8, "Declined action": "A slot for an action that was refused before it ran is filled by the decider's signed refusal bound to that action."; on 2026-10-08 Iman Schrock replied "the refusal should satisfy the decision slot, not fill the downstream effect slot", and that a verified refusal "can make that effect slot not applicable when the declaration names refusal as a terminal condition." On 2026-10-07 Pavel Izmaylov posted the individual draft draft-izmaylov-agent-permission-receipts: the principal signs a permission with a passkey that carries "limits a machine can check" and conditions, and a verifier states for each recorded action whether it stayed within that permission. Schrock replied on 2026-10-08 comparing it with the individual drafts draft-schrock-ep-authorization-receipts-13 and draft-schrock-ep-bounded-capability-receipts-06 and suggested a comparison in Section 11 of the draft. On 2026-09-30 a participant wrote on the list "Let me know if you want me to share some of our practices on EDR and Gateways during any interim or future meetings." (EDR: endpoint detection and response); on 2026-10-08 the lead editor of the expected-record draft answered "thank you for offering text, and yes please." and the participant wrote that the architecture draft and the charter should "identify the necessary PEPs that should be covered first, rather than jumping into defining the record entries directly" (the message does not expand PEPs; policy enforcement points is the usual expansion). On 2026-10-08 the lead editor of the expected-record draft wrote "Both cases go into the -00." (cases 7 and 8), added that the contributors of the two cases "will be named as contributors for these" (see Disclosure for the credit to the author of this map), and wrote "The draft will be draft-ahuja-schrock-audit-expected-records."; the datatracker page of that name returned 404 and the document search found no draft with "expected-record" in its name on 2026-10-09, so the text is pending and its content was not read. On 2026-10-11 a participant wrote a ninth case, "Refusal with an undetermined cause": "The slot is filled by a record that states whether a refusal came from a check that ran and failed, or from a check that", adding "AAE as published collapses both causes into a single DENY, so this case describes a gap in my own specification as much as anywhere else." Iman Schrock answered the same day (his text read as quoted in the lead editor's reply) that where the declaration requires grounds, "a single DENY cannot tell us whether revocation was established or the status check could not finish", and the lead editor of the expected-record draft wrote the same day "This goes into the -00 as Case 9, just like Iman put it. Lars will be named as a contributor for this case." On 2026-10-12 the same participant wrote that the decision receipt format that he publishes "carries Case 9 as fields". entries.name: IETF DAWN, Discovery of Agents With Names (working group)
entries.status: The IESG approved the DAWN charter on 2026-10-22 and the Working Group (WG) is active: the datatracker group history of that day records "Charter approved, group active", and the group page lists the approved charter as charter-ietf-dawn-01, posted on 2026-10-22 after charter revisions 00-11 and 00-12 (read 2026-10-23). Chairs: Dapeng Liu and Frank Brockners; technical advisor: Kehan Yao; Area Director: Éric Vyncke (Internet Area). The group history records "Chair changed to Dapeng Liu, Frank Brockners from Adrian Farrel, Wes Hardaker": Adrian Farrel and Wes Hardaker chaired the group while it was a BoF and a proposed WG, and were named as chairs of the proposed WG in the WG Review announcement of 2026-10-09. The approved charter says: "The DAWN working group will coordinate with WIMSE and OAUTH WGs as well as other WGs related to DNS (e.g., DNSSD), discovery, identities, or AI (e.g., AGENTPROTO). It will also coordinate with external standards bodies as necessary." Before the approval: the group changed from BoF to Proposed on 2026-08-24; charter 00-09 was on the IESG ballot in early October; charter 00-10 was in external review from 2026-10-09, with comments to the IESG due by 2026-10-19, and was on the agenda of the IESG telechat of 2026-10-22; on 2026-10-22 the "Approve" ballot was closed and the charter state changed to Approved.
entries.relevance: DAWN is chartered to standardise how a client discovers "public properties of AI resources", so it is the IETF venue where a seller's agent surface would be found. The charter gives three deployment contexts with one example each (approved charter charter-ietf-dawn-01, read on the datatracker on 2026-10-23; the same examples as in charter 00-10): for the local network "within the local network, e.g., discover all agents in this shop;", and for the public Internet "between cooperating parties with trust relationships over the public Internet, e.g., discover all agents of example.org, for all its customers/members.". The WG "will also specify the minimum public discovery information (e.g., type, reachability information, communication protocol, services)."; commerce as a scope item: not found in the approved charter charter-ietf-dawn-01, read 2026-10-23 (commerce, merchant, transaction, payment and purchase do not occur; "shop" occurs once, in the local network example "within the local network, e.g., discover all agents in this shop;"), nor in charter 00-10 (2026-10-13) and charter 00-08 (2026-10-03). On 2026-10-05 the INT Area Director wrote, on a request for a non-WG mailing list for DNS records under underscore labels that carry keys, key commitments or references to them, "While a mailing list will be created, I would like to push back on its name as it misses link to DNS"; the requester proposed the name dns-underscore-keys. An individual survey, draft-jimenez-dawn-discovery-landscape-00 (2026-07-03), compares discovery mechanisms from the IETF, AAIF, 3GPP and open-source projects and lists eight gaps, among them "Well-Known Namespace Pressure"; a text search of it finds no occurrence of AI Catalog, Agentic Resource Discovery (ARD), UCP or commerce (2026-10-06). The individual draft draft-zhang-dawn-agent-discovery-framework proposed a two-layer federated architecture in revision -07 (2026-10-15, text read 2026-10-16); revisions -08 (2026-10-19) and -09 (2026-10-21) followed, and the text of -09 was not read (datatracker, 2026-10-23). entries.name: IETF Web Bot Auth (webbotauth WG)
entries.status: Active Working Group (WG), listed for coordination by the draft W3C Agentic Web charter; the first WG draft, draft-ietf-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-00, was adopted on 2026-09-01, and a two-hour session was requested for IETF 127 on 2026-09-15. Implementation reports and proposed edits to the draft were on the list between 2026-10-04 and 2026-10-13. On 2026-10-13 the datatracker listed draft-ietf-webbotauth-httpsig-protocol-00 (2026-09-01) as the only WG draft, and it still did on 2026-10-26 (API: one draft in the group, revision 00). In the thread on updates to the crawler best practices draft a participant posted a revised text proposal on 2026-10-12 for a distinct Signature-Agent URL, key and key directory per crawler purpose, with pull requests in the WG draft repository and as PR #23 of garyillyes/cbcp. On 2026-10-22 PR #23 ("Identify crawler purposes with distinct Signature-Agent URLs") was merged and issue #3 of the same repository was closed as a duplicate; PR #140 of the WG draft repository, "Separate crawler and agent signing identities", which calls itself a companion to cbcp PR #23, was merged the same day; and revision -01 of the individual draft draft-illyes-webbotauth-cbcp was published (no stream, "I-D Exists", expires 2027-04-25). Its section 2.2 recommends "a distinct Signature-Agent URL, and therefore a distinct key directory, for each crawler purpose"; the text of -01 contains neither "429" nor "Retry-After", and PR #22 of garyillyes/cbcp, on those signals, was open on 2026-10-23. Also on 2026-10-22 the individual draft draft-kelley-webbotauth-sail-00, "SAIL: Source Address Identity List", was published: "a metadata format served at a well-known URI in which the operator of automated HTTP clients publishes the IP prefixes its services send from". On 2026-10-23 the datatracker recorded the webbotauth session at IETF 127 as "Waiting for Scheduling"; on 2026-10-26 the agenda of the meeting schedules it on Tuesday 2026-11-17, 16:30 to 18:30 San Francisco time (America/Los_Angeles, UTC-8), room Continental 4.
entries.relevance: The WG standardises cryptographic authentication of automated clients (HTTP message signatures, key directories), which a seller or its content delivery network (CDN) can use to tell which agent is calling. The chairs wrote on 2026-09-01 "Based on the feedback on the mailing list, the WG decided to adopt this draft as a WG document." Participants wrote of merchant-side verifiers: "We operate a production merchant-side verifier for automated commerce traffic (Web Bot Auth, Visa TAP, Google AP2)" (2026-08-03) and "We have implemented and use WBA for bot auth at Shopify in production, and we landed WBA interop for UCP" (2026-08-19). On 2026-10-04 a participant from Auth Your Agent reported an implementation in which a user withdraws an agent by serving its key directory with no keys, cut max-age from 3600 to 300 because "an hour is a long time when the agent has just bought something the user disputes", and asked that verifiers respecting Cache-Control become a normative SHOULD in section 5.5.2 (the draft's appendix C.4 says they "should respect Cache-Control"); Thibault Meunier replied on 2026-10-07 "It seems that the simpler solution would be to prevent the agent from making request in the first place." On 2026-10-08 a participant from Akamai, writing as a verifier, supported moving the C.4 guidance into section 5.5.2 as normative text and proposed "Verifiers SHOULD NOT treat a cached directory as fresh beyond its freshness lifetime as defined in Section 4.2 of [HTTP-CACHE], except as permitted by Section", adding that "short signature expires values (Section 6.3) act faster than any directory TTL". The same day a participant, who publishes per-agent keys as a DNSSEC-signed record set and deactivates an agent by removing its key, wrote that "Section 5.5.2 bounds the wrong thing": where the key set reaches a verifier as a signed artifact (section 5.5.3), "the bound is the Appendix B signature's expires rather than any cache lifetime", and he measured on his apex "TTL 300 seconds against a signature window of 14 days and 1 hour". He proposed a sentence for 5.5.2 on the signature's expires and noted that section 6.3 (removal as the only remedy) and appendix C.12 (manual key rotation as the only revocation mechanism, listed as an anti-pattern) read as a contradiction when taken together. that participant answered on 2026-10-08 that his directories sent max-age=300 while the Appendix B proof on each was valid for 7 days, that he had cut the proof to one hour with a re-signature every 15 minutes, and that he supported the text of the participant who publishes per-agent keys. On 2026-10-09 the same participant wrote that "The revocation thread got me reading the rest of the draft" and proposed for Appendix C.1 to replace "or the key is unknown" with "or the resolved directory does not provide the key", because a verifier could read an unknown key as "the key isn't on my list of bots" and so put a new agent that signs correctly in the same "unverified" outcome as a failed fetch; he also asked whether the draft should say anything about an intermediary that signs all its users' requests with one operator key, where removal under section 6.3 withdraws every user at once. On 2026-10-07 a participant asked whether two bots with different purposes from one operator should have distinct Signature-Agent values and proposed a statement "So it's clear different Signature-Agents need to be used for different purposes / use cases."; he wrote that section 4.1 makes the Signature-Agent URL the identifier. A participant from hCaptcha answered that it is similar to an open proposal, pull request #23 of garyillyes/cbcp, and that some crawl operators already do it, and wrote "I would support this proposal." On 2026-10-08 the same participant from Akamai supported a Signature-Agent per crawler purpose on the cbcp thread, citing that section 6.5 of the protocol draft "already says implementations SHOULD NOT reuse a signing key for different purposes and should use distinct keys and directories" and that "A signature that spans several purposes verifies fine but cannot carry that policy."; he asked that the 6.5 example be broadened to "an operator that runs both crawlers and user-directed agents". The crawler best practices draft (draft-illyes-webbotauth-cbcp, individual) was changed on 2026-10-05 (commit cc9942d of garyillyes/cbcp) and announced on the list the same day: a note that the practices "are intended for crawlers" and are "not necessarily appropriate for all automated clients", particularly "user-directed AI agents"; the requirement levels of the recommended practices changed from MUST to SHOULD; the proposal for a central crawler registry removed; and a Security Considerations section written, which says the opt-outs "are voluntary and do not constitute access control or content security measures" and that the User-Agent "is unauthenticated and trivially spoofed". It also defines two other TXT records, `_org-alter.<domain>` and `_alter.<domain>`. It is not adopted by a WG and is not counted among the discovery paths on the home page; its author proposed this addition in issue #22 of this map's repository and states being a co-founder of ~alter, which publishes an `_mcp` record for its own domain.

entries.name: Personal Agent Consent & Trust Protocol (PACT), published by Decagon with Instinct
entries.status: Version 1.0 of the specification ("This is PACT 1.0.") is published at openpactprotocol.org (the Decagon announcement is dated 2026-10-06), and the repository openpactprotocol/openpactprotocol (created 2026-10-01, Apache-2.0) holds the documentation, a reference Provider, a demo personal agent and conformance tests; its latest commit on main is 838c6bd (2026-10-06, a dependency update), read 2026-10-13. Decagon, 2026-10-06: it is open-sourcing PACT, "co-developed and supported by Instinct". No standards body or governing organisation is named in the pages of the site read on 2026-10-13.
entries.relevance: PACT builds on A2A 1.0 and defines how a personal agent identifies itself to a business's support agent and, optionally, which permissions the customer has granted it. The business's Agent Card is found at "https://{brandDomain}/.well-known/agent-card.json", which "serves the card or redirects to" the Provider's URL; the personal agent "never builds it from a Brand ID". The Poppy protocol uses a different well-known document (see pap and seam S1). The personal agent signs every request with a JWT (ES256 or RS256) checked against its published keys, and section 3.3 says what that proves: "That a known personal agent is calling for someone it calls sub. Not that sub owns a Brand account." Delegated authority is optional: the customer logs in with the business, never with the personal agent, and approves scopes that "Each Brand defines" (examples on the card: orders:read, orders:cancel), through OAuth 2.0 device code (RFC 8628). The Decagon post puts it as "It separates the identity of the personal agent from its authority to act on a customer". Section 5.6: every reply under a delegation token carries a signed receipt (grant id, user, scopes used, actions, timestamp), and "Personal agents SHOULD verify and keep receipts". The receipt records what the Provider's agent did; the words consumer, durable medium and confirm are not found in the specification page (2026-10-13).
entries.boundary: The specification does not define a registry: "This spec does not define a registry." Registration of a personal agent with a Provider is out of scope ("How these are exchanged is out of scope"), and each Brand defines its own scopes, none reserved by PACT.

entries.name: Personal Agent Protocol (PAP, "Poppy"), published by Sierra with Meta
entries.status: Draft 0.1 of the specification is published at personalagentprotocol.org (announced 2026-10-06, draft published 2026-10-09; the pages read on 2026-10-13 are marked "Updated Oct 12, 2026"), under the Apache License 2.0 with the names and the logo excluded; a further 35 design partners were named on 2026-10-09. Governance is worded two ways, not reconciled here. Sierra, 2026-10-06: "an open standard Meta and Sierra are developing along with industry partners at Genesys, Instinct, Rocket, Shopify, Stripe, and Walmart". Decagon, 2026-10-06: "join the Personal Agent Protocol working group announced by the team behind Meta's Muse to help shape an industry standard". No standards body or governing organisation is named in the pages of the site read on 2026-10-13. Read 2026-11-09, as of 2026-11-06: in the specification's repository (personal-agent-protocol/personal-agent-protocol, created 2026-10-14) version 0.2 was published on 2026-10-26 and version 0.3 on 2026-11-05, which opened draft 0.4; a reference implementation is not published by 2026-11-06, and the Demos page at the commit that published 0.3 lists demos "built by the community" that "have not been officially reviewed or endorsed by the Personal Agent Protocol authors or partners"; a public record of design workshops is not found (2026-11-09). Sierra's landing page now says "40+ design partners".
entries.relevance: Discovery is one well-known document: "A Company MUST publish its poppy.json document at https://{domain}/.well-known/poppy.json over HTTPS". The well-known URL "MAY redirect" to where the document is hosted, and "Personal Agents MUST follow redirects, and every redirect MUST be to an HTTPS URL"; the UCP specification says the opposite for its profile (see seam S1). poppy.json is not in the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) well-known URI registry (not found in the registry XML, 2026-10-13). The agent is identified by a URL: "A Personal Agent's client_id MUST be an HTTPS URL that returns its metadata document", which carries a jwks_uri and a token_endpoint_auth_method of private_key_jwt; the Company can register, allow-list, block or revoke client ids. The operations extension, section 8 ("What a confirmation proves"), says what a confirmation does not show: "It doesn't prove that the User saw the terms or approved them." The announcement of 2026-10-06 says the protocol "defines how personal agents interact with businesses": it "starts on the website, where a personal agent can discover what the company offers and how to reach it", the session "is built on OAuth", and the customer decides whether the agent has read-only or write access. Context, not part of the protocol: Retail Insight Network reported on 2026-09-23 that Shopify and Meta partnered so that Meta's assistant Muse can complete purchases across Shopify's merchants through Shop Pay.

entries.name: Shopify, MCP surfaces for buyer agents, developers and merchants
entries.status: Three distinct MCP surfaces are documented or published by Shopify: checkout for buyers' agents (server-side Checkout MCP and, since 2026-09-28, Checkout WebMCP), the local developer package @shopify/dev-mcp (latest version 1.16.0, 2026-09-25), and a remote MCP for merchants at setup.shopify.com/mcp. For the merchant surface the source is Shopify's own toolkit repository; no page on shopify.dev was found for it. A fourth surface is for shoppers' agents: the command-line client @shopify/shop (npm, MIT; version 1.0.3 published 2026-10-08, 01:20 UTC, after 1.0.2 on 2026-10-07), whose repository Shopify/shop has its latest commit d1e8c7c on main (2026-10-08, 01:17 UTC); neither the README, the skill file nor the transactions reference declares a beta or preview status or a list of supported countries (not found, 2026-10-13). Read 2026-11-09: the latest toolkit release is v2.3.0 (2026-10-27, Shopify Flow workflows through the Admin API), after v2.1.2 (2026-10-14) and v2.2.0 (2026-10-16, whose notes say the OpenAI plugin packages "an exact Shopify MCP configuration, and content-free UCP telemetry"); at the tag v2.3.0 the folder skills/ucp still holds SKILL.md and .cursor-plugin/mcp.json still declares the remote MCP at `setup.shopify.com/mcp`.
entries.relevance: Buyers' agents: the documentation says "Use Checkout WebMCP when your agent runs in the buyer's browser. If your agent can run on a server, then use Checkout MCP", and that Checkout WebMCP "implements the UCP checkout capability (dev.ucp.shopping.checkout)"; see ucp and browsers-webmcp. Developers: @shopify/dev-mcp is a local npm package (npm registry, read 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-13, version 1.16.0 published 2026-09-25). Merchants: Shopify-AI-Toolkit v2.1.0 (2026-10-01) states "The Cursor plugin, which Grok Bot also installs from the Cursor Marketplace, now connects to Shopify's remote MCP at `setup.shopify.com/mcp`"; the file .cursor-plugin/mcp.json at that tag declares an http server with that URL and an auth block with a client id, and v2.1.1 (2026-10-08) changes the plugin description to "Create and manage your store with Shopify". The toolkit release v2.0.1 says "Regenerated agent skills from @shopify/shopify-dev-tools 1.17.1"; the package @shopify/shopify-dev-tools returns E404 on the npm registry (2026-10-08 and 2026-10-13). Since v2.0.0 the toolkit publishes UCP as a separate skill: the CHANGELOG entry for 2.0.0 reads "UCP ships separately as `ucp`", and the folder skills/ucp at the tag v2.1.1 (commit 26d0623, 2026-10-08, 00:34 UTC) holds a SKILL.md named ucp whose description begins "Use when the user wants to use the UCP CLI to find, compare, buy, or track products from online merchants" and which requires the binary ucp (read 2026-10-13). Shopper's agents: the README of Shopify/shop (commit d1e8c7c, read 2026-10-13) says the command-line interface (CLI) "lets agents search millions of stores, build carts, check out and pay with the shopper's Shop account, and track orders" and is a client of Shop's MCP server at mcp.shop.com. It says: "Some stores have no agent checkout API (UCP); the agent has to enter a payment credential into the site's checkout form in a browser." For that case the shopper approves a "spend request" on Shop and the agent receives a one-time credential up to the approved limit; the skill file says "Prefer Shop/UCP checkout when available". The reference skills/shop/references/transactions.md says of the agent's report on the purchase "This records your report, not payment confirmation.", of a credential state "`consumed` without an `instrument` does not establish credential delivery or payment.", and of cancelling the request "this does not cancel/refund the purchase or revoke an issued credential." The core of the CLI is a compiled binary (lib/shop.wasm, about 1.9 MB), so its logic is not readable as source; the repository holds nine commits, all of 2026-10-07 and 2026-10-08. No call was made to any MCP or OAuth endpoint; only documentation, repositories and listings were read.

entries.status: Specification version 0.2, described in its text as "0.2: Draft" with status "RFC: Request for Comments"; the repository README calls it a Developer Preview launched on 23 June 2026, and the Python package agentrust-trace 0.11.0 was released on 2026-09-25. The README states that the specification is hosted at the Linux Foundation as "TRACE Specification, a Series of LF Projects, LLC", and a Linux Foundation press release of 2026-08-25 announces the contribution of TRACE from OPAQUE. Reading of 2026-10-13: the README of the repository now says "a proposal to bring it into the Agentic AI Foundation as a Sandbox project is in progress" and points to aaif/project-proposals issue #42, which is open with the label Under Review, 8 comments and a last update on 2026-10-02; the specification stays at v0.2 ("Spec v0.2 is current"), main is at commit 8562b09 (2026-10-13, 00:33 UTC), and the latest release objects are conformance-v0.6.2 (2026-10-03, the conformance test package) and v0.11.0 (2026-09-25, the Python package agentrust-trace 0.11.0, numbered apart from the specification). The folder spec/ also holds a draft named mcp-profile-v0.3-draft.md, not read. Reading of 2026-10-21: the README still says "Spec v0.2 is current" and still describes the AAIF Sandbox proposal as "in progress"; issue #42 is open, labelled Under Review, with 9 comments and a last update on 2026-10-15. In its last comment (2026-10-15) the filer, the project lead of TRACE, writes that the contributing entity is now "TRACE Specification, a Series of LF Projects, LLC" and that "OPAQUE Systems wound down on 12 October"; he also repeats a question of 2026-09-21 about a Technical Committee sponsor, and the issue shows no reply to it. These statements are the filer's own; no AAIF decision was read. MAINTAINERS.md now lists the Project Lead, two repository maintainers and two reviewers (since 2026-10-15); the two OPAQUE spec editors read on 2026-10-09 are no longer listed.
entries.relevance: The specification says "This is the rulebook for TRACE: it defines the Trust Record (a signed receipt describing one AI agent run), how records are anchored in a" The README describes TRACE as "an open format for a signed receipt of an AI agent run: what ran, where, under which rules, on what kind of data, and which" and states its limit: "A v0.2 signature proves who made a record and that it has not changed. It does not prove the hardware claims inside it". The specification text is under the Community Specification License 1.0 and the code under Apache 2.0 (LICENSE and README); GitHub's repository metadata reports the licence as NOASSERTION. MAINTAINERS.md lists as Project Lead Imran Siddique (AgenTrust-io), as spec editors Rishabh Poddar and Aaron Fulkerson (OPAQUE Systems), and two repository maintainers listed in the same file. The Linux Foundation press release says "The Linux Foundation will provide vendor-neutral governance for TRACE to support sustainability and long-term growth." In the AAIF Identity and Trust work TRACE is the format cited by the shared runner of agentrust-io/integrations, which validates "reference shapes" of the released package agentrust-trace 0.11.0, a reference package, not a version of the specification, which is v0.2 (see aaif-identity-trust).

entries.relevance: The AP2 mandates extension says businesses must "embed a cryptographic signature in checkout responses, proving the terms (price, line items) are authentic" and platforms provide mandates "proving the user explicitly authorized the specific checkout state and funds transfer". The Order page calls the entity "the authoritative latest state of the order at the time of retrieval or delivery", where webhook payloads "be signed by the business and verified by the platform". Terms travel in policies[] (PR #572, merged 2026-07-23), where the business states rules such as a refund window; the PR says "Policies never force display." On agent identity, the signatures page (PR #483, merged 2026-07-03) says a dual-audience signature "is the RECOMMENDED path for integrators" who want interoperability with Web Bot Auth verifiers; that interoperability is request-scoped. A food domain (`dev.ucp.food.checkout`, `food.fulfillment`) was proposed on 2026-10-03 for early feedback (PR #897, opened by a participant "On behalf of the entire Food Domain Tech Council"; its label on 2026-10-05 was status:needs-triage and on 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-13 is status:under-review, with gov:needs-tc-review and 12 comments on 2026-10-13). A proposal to authenticate the platform client through attestation (issue #852, opened 2026-09-22) was described by its author on 2026-10-04 as "now ready for Technical Council review". Issue #375 (2026-05-29) declined external place identifiers in the core schema: "Adding specialized reconciliation mappings to the core schema is a premature optimization." The Common capability `dev.ucp.common.ask` was merged on 2026-10-07 (PR #538; commit a41a2dc). Its page says "The Ask capability provides natural-language Q&A about a Business's resources, policies, and services." and "`ask` is the open-question complement to UCP's structured commerce capabilities". Two rules of its text: "A Business MUST NOT change the state of any resource exposed through another UCP capability or extension in response to an `ask` request." and "An answer is indicative, not authoritative."; where an answer conflicts with the representation returned by the capability that owns the resource, "that representation is authoritative and the Platform MUST prefer it", and "A Platform MUST NOT treat an `answer` as the binding disclosure for a safety, allergen, or regulatory claim." The page lists as typical use cases product questions ("fit, materials, compatibility, comparisons"), policy questions ("returns, shipping, warranty, refunds"), FAQ and how-to ("store hours, shipping timelines, accepted payment methods") and clarification about a specific resource, grounded in an identifier. The description of the pull request, not the specification, lists "policies, fit and suitability, materials, compatibility, amenities, support information, and Business-specific knowledge". The merge adds docs/specification/common/ask/ (index, Representational State Transfer (REST) and MCP bindings), docs/specification/shopping/ask/index.md and source/schemas/common/ask.json; text read at commit f2206e6 (the head of main on 2026-10-09; on 2026-10-13 main is at 9756aa9, and a git diff of the two commits shows no change to the overview, AP2 mandates, signatures, order, ask and lodging pages cited here). Pull request #811 (opened 2026-09-07 by a participant, open; among its labels on 2026-10-09 status:stale-review and gov:needs-tc-review; no comment or review; state and labels unchanged on 2026-10-13) proposes an optional `offers[]` array on the catalog variant "so one catalog can list a product sold by several different merchants and send each to the right seller's checkout". Each offer names its seller by `seller.domain`, the Merchant of Record, with the seller's own `item_id` and an authoritative price; the proposed schema text describes the domain as "The seller's canonical host: a bare hostname without scheme, path, port, or trailing slash" and adds "A Platform resolves this host to the seller's UCP profile at `/.well-known/ucp` and verifies its signing keys via authority binding." The overview page uses "canonical" for the host that serves a schema (lines 158 to 164); which of the bare and the www host is canonical for a profile is not found in the overview page at f2206e6 nor in the five files of the pull request (2026-10-09). The overview page says, in Profile Requirements, Hosting, item 2, "Profile endpoints MUST NOT use redirects (3xx)." (line 1466) and, in the rules for any URL dereferenced during identity resolution, item 2, "Implementations MUST NOT follow redirects (3xx)." (line 1514); line 182 applies the same rule to schema URLs (file at commit f2206e6 of 2026-10-07; unchanged at 9756aa9 on 2026-10-13). Items 3 and 4 of Hosting ask for a Cache-Control with public and a max-age of at least 60 seconds, and for a validator (ETag or Last-Modified). The well-known URI suffix `ucp` is registered in the IANA Well-Known URIs registry, status provisional, registered 2026-10-26, change controller Ilya Grigorik, reference the UCP overview (profile structure) (registry updated 2026-10-26, read 2026-10-27). The registration request (issue #92 of the registry's repository, opened 2026-06-06) was closed as completed on 2026-10-27. The profile rule first appears in commit 0426800 of 2026-02-17, "feat: signing for UCP requests & responses (#156)". The author of the census reported in issue #904 (2026-10-07, 2026-10-08) and Discussion #867 (comment 18810486, posted 2026-10-08) a census of 225 hosts probed from Seoul, one route and one attempt per host, 3xx not followed. Version of 2026-10-08, read in the edit history of the comment (figures declared by the source, not verified by this map): 62 positives (200, parses as JSON, ucp.version present), of which 58 Shopify and 4 not identified; declared versions 2026-08-25 (58), 2026-04-08 (3), 2026-01-23 (1); signing keys published by 0 of 62; the other rows: 1 refused by robots.txt, 7 responses 200 that did not parse, 12 3xx at the profile path, 65 404, 2 410, 59 403, 3 429/418/503, 14 connect, timeout or TLS failures. The author states "Not a random draw": a hand-built list of well-known storefronts plus the WooCommerce showcase, heavily Shopify-skewed, so the rate is not an adoption estimate; all figures declared by the source, not verified by this map. Four of the 62 positives have a home page answering 403 or 429 while the profile path answers 200 (comment of 2026-10-07, where the hosts are named). The author reports that probing the host as written gave 60 positives and 23 3xx, and that resolving the canonical host first gave 62 and 12. In the frame of #867 the 62 is "row 2 and ucp.version present", that is a floor on row 2 as the frame defines it (parses as JSON), with rows 3 and 4 not measured; the author of this map replied that the 7 non-parsing 200s are row 1 without row 2, whereas the run lists them among the cases it "could not ask". In Discussion #864 (Lodging), a participant who operates a small property asked on 2026-10-07 how a platform finds a property that is not in a global distribution system (GDS), a chain central reservation system (CRS) or a channel manager feed; the author of this map replied on 2026-10-08 that "today a property-hosted profile is necessary but not sufficient", and the same participant asked whether platforms will discover a profile on the property's own domain or receive lodging inventory only through connectivity partners; no maintainer reply was found among the discussion's six comments, the last of 2026-10-08 (read 2026-10-13). The lodging booking page says a platform "MUST supply valid property.id, and either a pre-composed stay.id OR both accommodation_type.id and rate_plan.id identifiers sourced from upper-funnel discovery mechanisms" (lines 426 to 428, commit f2206e6); the location_summary schema describes id as "Stable, opaque, Business-scoped Location identifier." Issue #678 (buyer consent at complete_checkout) was closed on 2026-10-07 with the merge of PR #883, and issue #666 (permalink and authenticated buyer session) the same day with the merge of PR #789, "require explicit buyer action before cart merge". In PR #691 (price_treatment, open) the author wrote on 2026-10-07 that after dropping not_asserted "an absent price_treatment and an absent tax now mean the same thing everywhere". Method note for censuses of /.well-known/ucp: WooCommerce PR #70679, merged on 2026-11-05 (milestone 11.4.0), fixes a discovery bug introduced by the PR that added the profile (#69886, merged 2026-10-16): requests other than GET and HEAD now get 405 with an Allow header, and the rewrite rule is checked on each request so that a store whose feature flag was set without the usual action no longer answers 404; PR #70680 (open on 2026-11-06) would serve the profile on stores using plain permalinks. A census run before these fixes reach a store may count a store with UCP enabled as having no profile; the release that ships them is not verified here. WooCommerce PR #69577 (open, draft on 2026-10-08) adds UCP catalog routes for search, lookup and product, implementing spec version 2026-04-08, off by default behind the woocommerce_ucp_enabled filter. Known Good posted in Discussion #867 on 2026-10-08, with the figures of https://knowngood.sh/standard/ucp, a run of 2026-09-26 to 2026-09-28 from AWS us-east-1 with robots.txt honoured and the user agent KnownGood-Verifier/0.3 (figures declared by the source, not verified by this map). Its population is 92,541 hosts that its crawl was allowed to ask, from its own index, "not a draw from storefronts". Rows of the frame as reported: HTTP 200 on 45,362 hosts (44,118 at the first request and 1,244 after a redirect), parses as JSON on 42,757, row 3 not measured ("Row 3 is empty on purpose."), and a protocol response (tools/list on the MCP endpoint named by the profile) on 41,424. By endpoint domain: myshopify.com 31,568, wixapis.com 9,782 and three singletons; "Merchant count 41,424; decision count 2" (two tool signatures cover 41,352 endpoints). The Known Good page says "Shopify and Wix advertise the MCP endpoint they run for every store through this profile". No page of Wix on UCP support was found (two searches, 2026-10-09), so Wix is a platform observed by Known Good only. The run follows 3xx at the profile path ("3xx followed up to 2 hops, https only, same registrable domain only"): 2,546 3xx, 2,188 followed, 1,244 ended in 200, and 286 cross-domain 3xx not followed; line 1514 of the overview page reads "Implementations MUST NOT follow redirects (3xx)." The 1,244 are reported here apart from the first-request count. The comment was edited on 2026-10-09 as a re-run of that day restructured against the frame, and its author wrote the same day (comment 18831816) that it was updated against the three points. Figures of the 9 October run (declared by the source, not verified by this map): 225 hosts and 675 requests (225 storefront requests to find the host the storefront settles on, 225 profile-path requests and 225 robots.txt requests), user agent string agentbi/0.1 (the prober's own), vantage KR (Seoul, AS45102); row 1 (HTTP 200) 68 hosts, row 2 and ucp.version present 62 (the source counted the two conditions as one figure until its run of 13 Oct, see below), rows 3 and 4 not measured, no validator run. It adds a run field for the probed host with the counts "seed host as written, www-normalised, other host in the same registrable domain"; a line for 3xx at the profile path, since "a profile reached only via a 3xx is never a positive"; a row 1a, "200 after redirect", counted "only if 3xx were followed; non-conforming, excluded from 2-4"; a prober-side line widened to "anything the prober chose not to send or could not finish"; and an optional hosting row H, "of row 2: Cache-Control public, max-age ≥ 60; ETag or Last-Modified". entries.relevance: The draft charter proposes a Working Group "to develop specifications that facilitate web pages and applications to be leveraged by LLMs and AI agents", scoped to site capabilities and context for agents, agent identity and delegation, and permissions and policies for agent actions. Until 2026-10-29 its one normative deliverable was WebMCP, adopted from the Web Machine Learning Community Group. At a943ce5 the normative deliverables are Site Capabilities for Agents (initial input: WebMCP), Agent Identity, Agent Delegation, Agent Interaction Measurement and Agentic Interaction Modes, with an Agentic Web Threat Model as another deliverable; the charter lists the Web Payment Security Interest Group (IG), IETF webbotauth and IETF aipref for coordination. On 2026-08-13 a representative of Apple wrote on PR #829 "Expect a formal objection if this is merged.", about the earlier plan to place WebMCP in the Web Machine Learning Working Group (WG). The W3C TAG Group Note "User Agents" (2026-10-22; the TAG is among the groups the draft charter lists for coordination) defines a user agent as "any software entity that interacts with websites outside the entity itself, on behalf of its user", names generative AI systems that act on the user's behalf among user agents, and sets the duties a user agent owes its user as protection, honesty and loyalty; it says "Collecting payment does not change to whom the duty of loyalty is owed" (read 2026-11-02). The Note is placed here rather than in an entry of its own because it is a statement, not a deliverable of a venue in this map, and this is the W3C venue where duties of agents acting on websites would land.

entries.name: W3C DID Resolution
entries.status: Candidate Recommendation Snapshot 2026-08-06; the latest Candidate Recommendation Draft is of 2026-11-03 (publication history on api.w3.org, read 2026-11-09, under the shortname did-resolution-1.0), after drafts of 2026-10-24, 2026-10-25, 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-30. The draft of 2026-10-01 (also 2026-08-28) marked the Decentralized Identifier (DID) URL dereferencing feature and sections 5, 6, 8 and 10 as at risk; the at-risk markings of the later drafts were not read. The exclusion opportunity on the Patent Review Draft ended on 2026-10-05. PR #344, "full pass at DID URL dereferencing algorithm (isolated)", was merged into main on 2026-10-13 at 02:10 UTC (merge commit 0956c93). The W3C publication history read on 2026-10-13 still lists the Candidate Recommendation Draft of 1 October 2026 as the latest, so no draft has been published after the merge; the merged text was not read for the at-risk markings. At the DID Working Group (WG) call of 2026-10-08 (minutes at w3.org/2026/10/08-did-minutes.html, read 2026-10-13) a chair ran the poll "PROPOSAL: Merge PR344 and agree that any future improvements to the DID URL Dereferencing Algorithm should be handled as separate issues.": eight participants recorded +1 and one recorded -1, "some technical issues not sufficiently discussed, charter violation, process violation, breaks compatibilty with DID 1.0 and CID". The chair then said "by Chair's decision, we will be merging this PR" and asked that the technical points be raised as separate issues; the merge followed on 2026-10-13. The minutes do not record the poll as a resolution. The PR comments of 2026-10-08 record the same dissent, that the changes violate the WG charter, and the chairs' answer that they do not. The statement of 2026-10-06 that unresolved points of the PR would be run as proposals so that objections can be recorded was followed by this single poll; separate issues for the points of the -1 were not looked for one by one on 2026-10-13.
entries.relevance: The specification defines how a DID is resolved to a DID document and how DID URLs are dereferenced; the relativeRef parameter is used for product-level references such as Digital Product Passports (issue #332). PR #344 (merged 2026-10-13) was described on 2026-10-02 as replacing the dereferencing algorithm with handlers and dropping built-in processing of relativeRef and serviceType (the latter from GS1); the merged text (38 commits, rebased on 2026-10-11) was not compared with that description; a participant wrote (https://github.com/w3c/did-resolution/pull/344#issuecomment-5611077919) "This breaks various existing deployments and use cases that I have explained on WG calls, e.g. in the area of Digital Product Passports." On 2026-10-05 a chair (Will Abramson) wrote that "the chairs plan to run a proposal to gauge the consensus of the group for merging this PR", and that otherwise "maybe the group has to start seriously considering ripping out dereferencing entirely from the specification." He approved the PR the same day ("Needs a rebase, but other than that looks good to me"). Exclusion opportunity closed 2026-10-05; no patent disclosures or exclusions listed on the DID WG intellectual property rights (IPR) page as of 2026-10-06. On 2026-10-07 a chair (Will Abramson) wrote on PR #344 "The chairs intend to run a proposal to adopt this PR and replace the existing DID URL Dereferencing section."; another participant approved the PR the same day, noting a concern about the MUST on giving the user the choice of resolvers, and a third participant wrote "I support the idea that we run a proposal to merge this PR on Thursday." On 2026-10-08 a participant wrote on the PR "In my opinion, the changes in this PR violate the WG charter" (and, he adds, like the previous "Resolve DID URLs" proposal) (comment 6060762625); the same chair answered the same day "In the chairs view, as has been stated numerous times on the calls, their is no charter violation." (comment 6062369708). On 2026-10-08 the same participant wrote that "The overloading of service type in this algorithm in my opinion requires a Class 4 change in DID 1.1, which is not allowed by the" (comment 6064294182). The same day that chair wrote for the chairs "My sense is the group is faced with two options", the first to "Adopt this PR as the new foundation for the DID URL Dereferencing algorithm" and the second to "Remove DID URL Dereferencing from this version of the specification" (comment 6062369708). In a review comment the chair wrote "This diagram needs to be updated to 2. Resolve the DID" (4220468912) and a participant answered "Ok. I can get that in today." (4221259495); commit 697f09b of 2026-10-08 by that participant, is titled "removed DID URL from dereferencing diagram". Merge: the PR was merged on 2026-10-13, 02:10:47 UTC (GitHub merge record, read 2026-10-14). PR #344 has no comment after 2026-10-08 (read 2026-10-13); the public-did-wg archive for October 2026 held three messages, the last of 2026-10-07, and the outcome of the call of 2026-10-08 is in its minutes (see the status).

entries.name: x402
entries.status: Open payment protocol under the x402 Foundation (Linux Foundation): intent announced 2026-04-02; operational launch and completed contribution by Coinbase announced 2026-07-14, with 40 member organisations at launch. On 2026-10-13 main is at commit 6c470a8 and the core specification header reads "Protocol Version: 2" (specs/x402-specification-v2.md); no release is listed on GitHub (not found, 2026-10-13). The file ROADMAP.md, which read "(update coming soon)" on 2026-10-03, was removed from main on 2026-10-13 by PR #3789, "chore: remove outdated ROADMAP.md and PROJECT-IDEAS.md". Correction: PR #8 of the Domain Discovery working group and PR #2979 of the core repository answered 404 on 2026-11-02, when version 1.3 of this map called them no longer reachable; on 2026-11-09 both are reachable again and open, with the same author; why they were unreachable is not known. Issue #11 of wg-domain-discovery, on the content of `/.well-known/x402`, is open (last comment 2026-10-31); a record of the working group call of 2026-11-02 announced in that thread is not found on GitHub (issue, repository files and the organisation's repositories, 2026-11-09). PR #4 of the working group, which proposes a small entry at `/.well-known/x402` linking to OpenAPI documents, is open.
entries.relevance: The README says "x402 is an open standard for internet native payments."; the server answers 402 with a PAYMENT-REQUIRED header, the client replies with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE, and an http-message-signatures extension identifies the paying agent. The offer-and-receipt extension lets the server "cryptographically commit to the payment terms it presents in" accepts[] (the payment terms of the offer, not the commercial terms of the sale) and sign a receipt; it says "Wire shape and field placement are not considered stable".
